title: Fuel Report November 2026
summary: Diesel prices remain elevated heading into November, with regional differences and ongoing crude oil market volatility keeping fuel costs firmly on carriers' radar.
body_markdown:
Fuel remains one of the highest[variable costs](http://truenorthfleet.com/articles/business/cost-per-mile-calculator) for owner-operators. Each month, we track the latest EIA diesel prices, regional spreads, and market forces affecting what you're paying at the pump, then break down what those numbers mean for your next load.


## National Diesel Price Updates


**Current national diesel price** : $6.29/gal, as of Nov 2, 2026


The national average fell 6 cents in the[latest EIA report](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/) , marking a modest pullback after prices climbed through much of October. However, diesel remains higher than this time last year, keeping pressure on carrier operating costs.


## Regional Breakdown: Where Prices Are Moving


Regional diesel prices declined across every major U.S. region in the latest EIA report. The Midwest posted the largest decrease, while the West Coast continued to have the highest prices.


Since last week…


- **DOWN:** Gulf Coast, Midwest, East Coast, Rocky Mountain, and West Coast
- **UP:** None
- **BIGGEST MOVE:** Midwest, down $0.08/gal


Regional price breakdown shows the highest prices on the West Coast and the lowest on the Gulf Coast. The difference between the **lowest- and highest-priced regions is currently $1.37/gallon** .


For a truck burning approximately 100 gallons, that's a **$137 difference per fill-up** , before considering taxes,[discounts](http://truenorthfleet.com/articles/business/fuel-cards) , or individual truck-stop pricing.


Source:[U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/) . *As of publish date.


## What's Driving Current Diesel Prices


[This month, keep an eye on](https://www.fleetowner.com/emissions-efficiency/news/55416288/us-diesel-and-gas-prices-decline-but-trucking-fuel-costs-remain-elevated-year-over-year) crude oil prices, Strait of Hormuz developments, and geopolitical tensions affecting global oil supplies.


## The November Fuel Outlook


Diesel prices enter November with some short-term relief, but significant uncertainty remains.[Tensions surrounding Iran](https://www.fleetowner.com/emissions-efficiency/news/55416288/us-diesel-and-gas-prices-decline-but-trucking-fuel-costs-remain-elevated-year-over-year) and the Strait of Hormuz continue to influence global oil markets. For carriers, that means fuel should remain a key consideration when calculating load profitability and deciding where and when to fuel.
